diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the nonsmooth case, we can choose the normalized $x_1$, respectively, $x_n$, in the eigenspace of $\lambda_{\max}(\cDo (d))$, respectively $\lambda_{\min}( \cDo (d))$.
The characterization for $\kappa$-optimally diagonally preconditioned matrix $A$ follows from solving $\nabla \kappa(e)=0$.
Let $1\leq k\leq n$ and $\lambda_k$ be a singleton eigenvalue with right and left eigenvector $x_k,y_k$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem asserts an iff characterization and its final sentence extends it to the nonsmooth case via eigenvector choices in the extreme eigenspaces. The proof covers only the differentiable case: it uses singleton-eigenvalue calculus (lem:eigderiv, lem:optkappacond) and solves $\nabla\kappa(e)=0$. In the nonsmooth case the 'if' direction survives (a vanishing single-pair quasisubgradient implies optimality via Cor Translation), but the 'only if' direction is false. Counterexample (n=3): $A = I - c\,vv^T$ with $v=(1,1,1)^T/\sqrt3$, $0<c<1$. The top eigenspace is $v^\perp$ (eigenvalue 1, double) and the bottom eigenvalue $1-c$ is simple with eigenvector $v$. Since $\tfrac12(u_1\bullet u_1 + u_2\bullet u_2) = v\bullet v = (1/3,1/3,1/3)$ for the orthonormal basis $u_1=(1,-1,0)/\sqrt2$, $u_2=(1,1,-2)/\sqrt6$ of $v^\perp$, Lemma Refined Quasisubdiff puts $0$ in the quasisubdifferential of $\kappa(\cDo(\cdot))$ at $d=e$, so $e$ is a global minimizer: $A$ is $\kappa$-optimally diagonally preconditioned. Yet no $w\in v^\perp$ satisfies $w\bullet w = v\bullet v$: it would force $|w_i|=1/\sqrt3$ for all $i$ and $w_1+w_2+w_3=0$, impossible for $w_i=\pm1/\sqrt3$. Hence no eigenspace choice meets the displayed condition at an optimum, contradicting the stated 'only if'.

failure_location.quote: Hence, $A$ is $\kappa$-optimally diagonally preconditioned if, and only if, the orthonormal eigenvector pair satisfies

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $\lambda_{\max}(\cDo(d))$ and $\lambda_{\min}(\cDo(d))$ are simple, prove the iff in that regime, and restate the nonsmooth case correctly: eigenspace choices give only a sufficient condition; the exact nonsmooth condition is $0\in (1/\lambda_n)\partial\lambda_{\max} + (\lambda_1/\lambda_n^2)\partial(-\lambda_{\min})$ (convex combinations of squared eigenvectors over the extreme eigenspaces), not a single eigenvector pair with $x_1\bullet x_1 = x_n\bullet x_n$.
issues.overall_effect: The characterization is unreliable whenever an extreme eigenvalue of the scaled matrix is multiple: an optimally preconditioned matrix can fail the eigenvector test, so the theorem cannot certify non-optimality in the nonsmooth case. The smooth-case characterization, the subgradient formulas, the algorithms, and the convergence theorems (which use only the sufficient direction and subgradient inclusions) are unaffected.
issues.title: Nonsmooth-case extension of the kappa-optimality characterization in Theorem optcondkappa is false
issues.why_classification: A central characterization theorem is false in a regime its statement explicitly claims to cover; the repair must either exclude that regime or replace the condition with a subdifferential-based one (a contained but nontrivial change). It is not serious because the smooth-case result, the sufficient direction, and all algorithmic and convergence guarantees survive unchanged, and no labelled result depends on the false direction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: since \Cref{GD} is a subgradient method, in general it is not a descent method

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes only the $\underline{\lim}$ statement (via Theorem 1 of kiwiel2001convergence). The appended 'in particular, $\kappa(\cDo(d_k))\downarrow\kappa_*$' claims monotone decrease of the objective values to $\kappa_*$, which neither follows from $\liminf=\kappa_*$ nor holds for subgradient methods — the paper itself states GD 'is not a descent method'. The theorem defines the running minimum $\kappa_*^j$ and never uses it, indicating the intended (correct) claim was $\kappa_*^j\downarrow\kappa_*$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the clause with the supported statement that the running-best values $\kappa_*^j=\min_{k\le j}\kappa(\cDo(d_k))$ decrease to $\kappa_*$, or delete it.
issues.overall_effect: Only the appended monotone-convergence clause is unreliable; the liminf/asymptotic-optimality guarantee for Algorithm GD stands, and no other result uses the clause.
issues.title: Unsupported monotone-descent clause appended to the subgradient convergence theorem
issues.why_classification: A one-clause correction with no new mathematics; the theorem's substantive guarantee and all dependents are preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Projecting onto it is also easy since it is just a simplex.

issues.failure_explanation: By eq: Simplex Def, $\hat\Omega$ is defined by $n-1$ coordinate lower bounds $v_i\ge\sqrt2(\hat\delta-1)$ AND the halfspace $\sum_i v_i\le-\sqrt2(\hat\delta-1)$. It is a simplex, not a box: with $l=\sqrt2(\hat\delta-1)<0$, the point $v=(M,l,\ldots,l)$ with $M$ large satisfies every lower bound but violates the sum constraint, so the sum bound is not implied by componentwise bounds. The paper itself describes the same set two pages earlier as 'just a simplex'.

failure_location.quote: it is easy to see that the set $\hat \Omega$ is just a box so it is a convex compact set that is easy to project onto

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'just a box' with the correct description of $\hat\Omega$ (a simplex: coordinate lower bounds plus one sum upper bound), consistent with the earlier 'it is just a simplex' remark.
issues.overall_effect: A reader implementing the projection in step Descent Nonh as a componentwise (box) projection on the strength of this sentence would leave the feasible set $\{v: e+Vv\ge\hat\delta e\}$, breaking the feasibility invariant on which Subgrad V's analysis relies. The surrounding conclusions (convex, compact, easy projection) remain true.
issues.title: Constraint set Omega-hat misdescribed as a box (it is a simplex)
issues.why_classification: A local correction of a false geometric description; no theorem, rate, or guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: And stationarity (optimality) of $\ocDo d))$ at $d=e$ is characterized by the gradient being zero, or equivalently by
a matrix $A$ that is $\kappa$-optimal with respect to diagonal preconditioning, i.e., the $\kappa$-optimal diagonal scaling for $A$ is the identity

issues.failure_explanation: The predicate '$A$ is $\omega$-optimal' is never defined. The paper's parallel usage ('a matrix $A$ that is $\kappa$-optimal ... i.e., the $\kappa$-optimal diagonal scaling for $A$ is the identity') forces the reading 'the $\omega$-optimal diagonal scaling for $A$ is the identity', under which the claim is false: by thm:optomegacomp, $d=e$ is $\omega$-optimal for $A$ iff $\diag A = (\trace A/n)e$, so e.g. $A=[[1,\rho],[\rho,1]]$ with $\rho\ne0$ is $\omega$-optimally diagonally preconditioned yet is not a multiple of $I$. The corollary's proof (AM-HM equality conditions) supports only the different, true statement that $\nabla\omega(A)=0$ (i.e. $\omega(A)=1$, the global minimum over $\Snpp$) iff $A=\alpha I$, which contradicts the diagonal-preconditioning reading and makes the stated 'i.e.' claim unusable as written.

failure_location.quote: i.e.,~$A$ is $\omega$-optimal if, and only if, it is a multiple of the identity

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword to an unambiguous true statement, e.g. '$\omega(A)=1$ (equivalently $\nabla\omega(A)=0$) iff $A=\alpha I$', and state separately that $A$ is $\omega$-optimally diagonally preconditioned iff $\diag(A)=(\trace A/n)e$.
issues.overall_effect: The final claim of the corollary is ill-defined and, under the paper's own convention for 'optimal A', contradicts thm:optomegacomp's characterization (constant diagonal). No formal result relies on it; the corollary's main content (Jacobi scaling) and its use in sect:optkappimprovomega remain valid.
issues.title: Corollary omegaoptDAD's 'A is omega-optimal iff multiple of the identity' is ill-defined and false under the paper's own terminology
issues.why_classification: A local rewording/clarification; the substantive content (Jacobi scaling, gradient characterization) and all uses survive unchanged.
